title: AM-DGCNN: Leveraging Graph Attention Networks and Edge Attributes for Link Classification in Knowledge Graphs
problem: Knowledge graphs often have incomplete link information, and existing DGCNN models lack the capability to process edge attributes, resulting in poor classification accuracy for knowledge graph link prediction.
motivation: Knowledge graphs are increasingly used to store and manage information, but their incompleteness limits practical utility; accurate link classification enables prediction and verification of missing connections.
method: To predict missing connections in knowledge graphs, the model identifies the local area around each potential link, called an enclosing subgraph. It uses attention mechanisms—methods that learn to assign different importance to edges based on their properties. By using graph attention networks (which learn variable weights for each edge) instead of graph convolution networks (which weight all edges equally), the model can better use the information stored in edge attributes to make predictions.
key_novelty: Replacing graph convolution networks with graph attention networks to enable the use of edge attributes for knowledge graph link prediction.
contributions: Proposes AM-DGCNN model that augments DGCNN with Graph Attention Networks to incorporate edge attributes
Achieves up to 99% AUC and 97% precision on knowledge graph link classification tasks
Demonstrates improved link classification performance over baseline DGCNN by better utilizing edge information
primary_theme: Graph attention networks for knowledge graph completion
